question: In young children (under 8 years), the narrowest part of the airway is the subglottis at the level of the cricoid ring, not the vocal cords as in adults.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is true. In adults, the vocal cords are the narrowest point and a cuffed ETT seals in the trachea. In children under 8, the cricoid ring is narrowest — hence the use of uncuffed tubes and precise size selection using age-based formulae.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Because the cricoid ring is the narrowest point in children, an appropriately-sized uncuffed ETT forms a natural seal there. Over-sizing risks pressure necrosis of the mucosa — a much greater hazard than in adults.
